item.title: 2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests: Border Guard Bangladesh deploys 95 platoons across seven districts, including two battalions in Gopalganj, stepping up surveillance at key installations and industrial zones using drones and police… / Several garment factories in Gazipur, Bangladesh, declare holidays amid ongoing minimum wage protests, as clashes erupt between workers and police along the Dhaka–Mymensingh Highway, with workers…
item.description:
Image: The Daily Star

Border Guard Bangladesh deploys 95 platoons across seven districts, including two battalions in Gopalganj, stepping up surveillance at key installations and industrial zones using drones and police body cameras.

Sources: The Daily Star

Several garment factories in Gazipur, Bangladesh, declare holidays amid ongoing minimum wage protests, as clashes erupt between workers and police along the Dhaka–Mymensingh Highway, with workers throwing bricks and police firing tear gas and stun grenades while Special Response Battalion, Ansar, BGB, and Industrial Police personnel deploy to the area.

Sources: The Business Standard

item.description:
Image: The Business Standard

Border Guard Bangladesh deploys 90 platoons across seven districts, with four more on standby, amid ongoing political violence and strike action.

Sources: Dhaka Tribune

Laid-off garment workers in Rupganj, Narayanganj District, block roads by felling trees and burning tires over unpaid wages.

item.title: Aftermath of the July Uprising: Border Guard Bangladesh deploys 97 platoons across seven districts, with five more on standby, amid ongoing political violence and labour unrest. / In Bangladesh, banned Awami League members loot and burn properties in Gopalganj District, including BNP MP Md.
item.description:
Image: The Guardian

Border Guard Bangladesh deploys 97 platoons across seven districts, with five more on standby, amid ongoing political violence and labour unrest.

Sources: The Guardian, The Daily Star

In Bangladesh, banned Awami League members loot and burn properties in Gopalganj District, including BNP MP Md. Selimuzzaman Mollah's ancestral home, a police station, and a Grameen Bank branch, and vandalise BNP and Jamaat-e-Islami properties. Separately, attackers burn the homes of former politicians Rahim Ullah in Feni District, Shahriar Alam in Rajshahi District and Mahmud Hasan Sumon in Mymensingh District.

Sources: BSS, The Financial Express

Image: The Business Standard

In Kafrul, Dhaka, police fire around ten stun grenades against demonstrating garment workers following clashes with Bangladesh Nationalist Party activists who allegedly harassed female factory employees, causing workers to stage demonstrations and halt production at several nearby garment factories.

Sources: The Business Standard

In Gazipur, Savar, and Ashulia, Bangladesh, thousands of garment workers demanding a monthly minimum wage increase from ৳12,500 (US$100) to ৳30,000 ($240) block the Dhaka–Mymensingh Highway and set fire to a police vehicle, causing police to fire tear gas and stun grenades in Gazipur and Ashulia as 55 factories close across the three areas, while police report around 300 arrests across 24 cases filed in Savar and Ashulia during the protests.

Sources: The Daily Star
